records.title: Decompression Procedures for Flying After Diving, and Diving at Altitudes Above Sea Level: Validation Tests
records.locator: FAD-I Tables 12–14, printed pp. 22–24 (PDF pp. 27–29). FAD-II Tables 17–19, printed pp. 29–31 (PDF pp. 34–36)
records.note: Nine dive profiles with subsequent two-stage chamber flights. In FAD-I, exclusion of flights stopped because of the partner's endpoint or equipment problems leaves 59 participants and 110 evaluable exposures. Five pain-only clinical aborts affected four people. FAD-II reports 28 participants and 57 exposures, including one possible atypical Type I event. VGE-triggered stops truncate observation.

observations.note: Repeat exposures in the same study participants. VGE-triggered stops shortened observation. Itching is a separate endpoint. The source provides no common delayed follow-up risk set. Paired stopping could exclude a second volunteer's result.
observations.outcome_window: During the staged altitude exposures until flight abort or scheduled conclusion.

records.title: Experimental trials to assess the risks of decompression sickness in flying after diving
records.locator: Historical discussion citing reference 11, printed p. 432 (PDF p. 2)
records.note: Vann's historical discussion cites SAM-TR-82-47 and reports the same 167 combined exposures. The text repeats the 60-fsw and 16,000-ft combination and describes the possible 14,250-ft event as DCS. Its own later recreational study used distinct participants, schedules and altitude.

records.title: Flying after diving: Validation tests for military divers
records.locator: Original AsMA abstract 158, printed p. 411 (PDF p. 27)
records.note: The later abstract reports 110 and 57 exposures with the same dive and altitude stages and matching rounded flight outcomes. It lists 20 different participants in each series, compared with 59 and 28 in the original report. The difference remains unresolved. Its FAD-II pain-only statement omits the original possible-status footnote.
